architecture_decisions: The architecture decision is to bind admitted validation profiles to server-owned, prequalified, source-free execution snapshots rather than assuming one existing snapshot is suitable for every ecosystem.
work_items: The work item is to implement the architecture decision by binding admitted validation profiles to server-owned, prequalified, source-free execution snapshots.
validations: The validation is to ensure that the architecture decision is implemented correctly by binding admitted validation profiles to server-owned, prequalified, source-free execution snapshots.

AC-01: validate protected requirement — `python-v1`, `node-v1`, and `dotnet-v1` resolve only through a finite server-owned mapping. Python and Node retain the existing common snapshot; .NET requires its dedicated snapshot. Unknown profiles, malformed IDs, and missing required .NET configuration fail closed. User/model/repository values cannot select snapshot identity.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — Candidate and accepted-lineage Python and Node validation continue to restore the existing compatible common snapshot, preserve their established fixed commands/evidence, and pass inherited protected execution tests. Production preflight also proves the common snapshot retains the already-admitted Node executable.

AC-03: validate protected requirement — `dotnet-v1` candidate and accepted-lineage execution use only the configured dedicated .NET snapshot. They never silently reuse the Python/Node common snapshot when the .NET snapshot is absent or invalid.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — For identical admitted profile/configuration, disposable candidate validation and accepted-lineage BUILD/TEST/VERIFY record the same exact snapshot ID alongside the same validation profile ID/digest.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — Production build preflight restores every production-enabled snapshot with deny-all network, verifies exact snapshot identity, verifies the fixed readiness probes required by the profiles mapped to that snapshot (`python` dependency probe plus `node --version` for the common snapshot and `dotnet --info` for the .NET snapshot), and rejects any snapshot containing repository source.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — The change does not add per-run SDK installation, generic shell commands, broader package domains, application credentials, source mutation authority, provider/deployment authority, or REVIEW bypass. .NET restore remains the existing fixed bounded PREPARE followed by verified deny-all BUILD/TEST/VERIFY.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — After a .NET-qualified snapshot is provisioned, configured, exact release source is deployed READY, and production preflight passes, the QA-owned source-only Project bound to `github:Ryan9876/ot-time` progresses through PLAN, IMPLEMENT, BUILD, TEST, VERIFY to REVIEW and its authenticated exact-lineage ZIP handoff verifies with no Vercel application deployment, repository-provider authorization dependency, out-of-band source edit, owner impersonation, or DB mutation.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — The governed provisioning mechanism produces an immutable .NET-qualified execution artifact from a fixed server-owned recipe, verifies the intended toolchain before publication, persists no Project/application source or reusable credentials, and cannot be invoked as part of a user Engineering Run or used to widen runtime command/network authority.
risks: The risk is to ensure that the architecture decision is implemented correctly by binding admitted validation profiles to server-owned, prequalified, source-free execution snapshots.

critique: The specification does not explicitly address the requirement for a qualified .NET snapshot identity for `dotnet-v1` execution, which is necessary for production preflight and authenticated exact-lineage ZIP handoff. This omission could lead to potential issues in the production environment, such as incorrect toolchain selection or inconsistent snapshot usage.
